problem:
Meridian Bank wants to offer a corridor for small exporters who sell from India to buyers in Europe. Today a payment from a European buyer to an Indian exporter travels through a chain of correspondents, takes days, and gives neither side a reliable status. The exporter, Kaveri Textiles, ships fabric to a buyer in the Netherlands and waits for euros to arrive before it can pay its own suppliers in rupees. The buyer wants to pay instantly in euros, the exporter wants rupees quickly, and both want to know where the money is at every step.

The corridor has to join two very different domestic worlds. On the India side the domestic legs run on rails that operate 24x7x365: UPI for small instant transfers, IMPS for instant bank transfers typically capped by banks around Rs 5 lakh, NEFT in half-hourly batches, and RTGS for individual real-time settlement with a minimum of Rs 2 lakh and no RBI maximum. On the Europe side the euro leg can run as an SCT Inst payment with a 10-second maximum execution window and no scheme-level maximum, or as a One-Leg-Out Instant Credit Transfer where one leg sits outside SEPA.

Between the two domestic systems sit currency conversion, compliance screening, data translation, liquidity and settlement. No single rail covers the whole journey, so the bank must design a bridge that orchestrates the legs, owns the FX risk window, and gives the customer one truthful status instead of a patchwork of local confirmations.
solution:
Design the corridor as an orchestration layer over independent legs, not as a single payment. The euro leg, the bridge settlement leg and the INR leg each have their own state machine, timeout and confirmation rule, and the orchestration state only moves to Complete when the required leg confirmations have all arrived. The euro leg uses SCT Inst inside SEPA or the EPC One-Leg-Out Instant Credit Transfer where one leg sits outside SEPA, under the Rulebook 2025 version 1.1 effective 5 October 2025. The INR leg uses the rail that fits the amount and urgency: UPI for small instant transfers within its limits, IMPS for instant bank transfers, NEFT for batched settlement, or RTGS for large individual real-time settlement from Rs 2 lakh.

Bind every payment to an FX quote contract that records the quote ID, currency pair, amount, rate, expiry and tolerance. Revalidate the quote at execution, and if the rate or amount has moved beyond tolerance, pause for a fresh quote and fresh customer consent. Store the quote snapshot and the consent evidence with the payment record so any later dispute can be reconstructed.

Compliance is designed into the corridor, not added after it. Sanctions, AML and fraud screening run with synchronous decision deadlines, and the corridor defines which checks are mandatory before release and which monitoring may follow the payment where the rules permit. Routing is validated against current, effective-dated reference data for correspondents, currencies, cut-offs and liquidity, and an approved alternate route is used only when policy permits it. Data is translated through a canonical model that preserves the structured or hybrid address, the purpose code and the identifier semantics of each rail, so nothing needed downstream is lost in translation.

decision.question: Kaveri Textiles is expecting EUR 40,000 from a Dutch buyer. The euro leg is accepted instantly, but the INR leg has not yet been confirmed and the FX quote is close to expiry. The learner must decide how the bridge should behave.

options.label: A
options.detail: Report the payment as complete because the euro leg was accepted.

options.label: B
options.detail: Hold the end-to-end status at In progress, keep each leg state separate, and revalidate the FX quote before releasing the INR leg.

options.label: C
options.detail: Cancel the euro leg and ask the buyer to send the payment again by correspondent banking.

options.label: D
options.detail: Execute the INR leg at whatever rate applies when it is processed, without telling the customer.

decisionRationale: Option B is correct because the corridor is only complete when every leg confirms, and an FX quote must be revalidated at execution. Option A is wrong because euro acceptance does not prove INR credit. Option D is wrong because executing at an unagreed rate breaks the quote contract and the consent evidence. Option C is wrong because cancelling a successfully accepted leg without a scheme basis creates unnecessary cost and delay.

steps.title: Instructs a EUR payment to Kaveri Textiles from European online banking, with invoice reference and purpose.
Validates the instruction, runs Verification of Payee on the euro leg, and obtains an FX quote for EUR to INR.
Accepts the FX quote, rate and expiry, and confirms the payment.
Runs sanctions, AML and fraud screening with synchronous decision deadlines and records each outcome.
Releases the euro leg as an SCT Inst or One-Leg-Out instant payment and awaits the beneficiary PSP confirmation.
On euro confirmation, revalidates the FX quote and confirms settlement liquidity for the INR leg.
Executes the INR leg on the selected domestic rail and confirms credit to the exporter account.
Matches all leg confirmations, updates the end-to-end status to Complete, and issues a single customer timeline.
Views the completed payment with the applied FX rate, fees and confirmation time for each leg.

happy: The buyer accepts the FX quote and confirms the payment. Screening clears within its deadlines, the euro leg is accepted and confirmed inside the 10-second SCT Inst execution window, and the bridge revalidates the quote while it is still valid. The Indian partner bank executes the INR leg on the selected domestic rail and confirms credit to Kaveri Textiles. The orchestration layer matches the euro confirmation, the FX execution and the INR credit, marks the corridor payment Complete, and both customers see one coherent timeline with the applied rate, the fees and the time of each leg.

negative.title: Correspondent or route unavailable
negative.detail: The selected route is temporarily unavailable or no longer supports the currency or corridor. Re-evaluate routing against current effective-dated reference data, use an approved alternate route only if policy permits, otherwise queue or reject with a transparent reason and never silently change settlement details.

negative.title: FX quote expires before execution
negative.detail: A delay pushes execution past the quote validity window. Block execution at the expired quote, obtain a fresh quote, and seek fresh consent if the rate or amount moves beyond tolerance. Record the expired quote and the new consent as separate audit events.

negative.title: Compliance screening threatens the instant SLA
negative.detail: A mandatory check cannot complete inside the rail processing window. Apply the approved fail-closed rule for mandatory controls, hold the payment with a clear reason, escalate within the screening SLA, and never bypass screening to protect the speed target.

negative.title: INR leg confirms late or not at all
negative.detail: The euro leg is confirmed but the domestic INR confirmation is delayed or missing. Keep the end-to-end status at In progress or Unknown, do not report completion, place the item in the corridor investigation queue, and resolve it through leg-level reconciliation before any compensation or retry.

technical: Build a canonical payment model that carries the instruction ID, end-to-end ID and UETR where applicable unchanged across the corridor, with separate fields for each rail reference so identifiers are never collapsed into one generic field. Preserve the structured or hybrid address with Town Name and Country Code as a minimum, and never teach a fixed structured-address cut-off date, since the timeline was extended and a new timeline was expected by December 2026. Keep FX quote, consent, screening decision and leg confirmation as separate durable events with timestamps and source systems. Make the INR leg posting idempotent on the corridor transaction ID so a duplicate callback cannot double-credit the exporter. Version all routing and reference data with effective dates, and record the route decision factors for every payment. Note that PSD2 remains the law in force; PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation are not law, with full application only around 2028, so corridor compliance must be built on PSD2.

accounting: Each leg posts its own linked accounting entries so the euro receipt, the FX conversion, the bridge settlement and the INR payout reconcile independently and in total. The euro leg credits a corridor settlement account on confirmation, the FX execution posts the conversion at the agreed rate with any spread recorded separately, and the INR leg debits the settlement account and credits the exporter. Any leg that confirms without its counterpart goes to a corridor suspense worklist with an owner and an SLA, and no compensation is posted until the leg states are established. Operations monitors quote expiries, route failures, screening holds and unmatched leg confirmations as separate queues, and nostro and settlement account reconciliation runs on the bridge accounts daily with same-day break ageing. Fees are disclosed per leg and posted as separate entries so the customer can see what each stage cost.

scenarios.given: a corridor payment with an accepted FX quote
scenarios.when: execution is attempted after the quote has expired
scenarios.then: the payment is not executed at a different rate. a fresh quote and fresh consent are requested before execution

scenarios.given: the euro leg is confirmed but the INR leg confirmation is absent
scenarios.when: the corridor timeout threshold is reached
scenarios.then: the end-to-end status moves to Unknown and enters investigation. the payment is not reported as Complete and is not blindly resubmitted

questions.question: Which euro mechanism covers the euro leg of a cross-border instant payment where one leg sits outside SEPA?
questions.explanation: The EPC One-Leg-Out Instant Credit Transfer covers the euro leg where one leg sits outside SEPA, under Rulebook 2025 version 1.1 effective 5 October 2025.

questions.question: What is the minimum amount for an RTGS payment in India?
questions.explanation: RTGS settles individually in real time with a minimum of Rs 2 lakh and no RBI maximum.

questions.question: What is the current legal status of PSD3?
options: It is law and PSD2 is repealed
It is not law; PSD2 remains in force
It applies only to instant payments
questions.explanation: PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation are not law. PSD2 remains in force, with full application of PSD3 only around 2028.

questions.question: How should the corridor report a payment whose euro leg is confirmed but whose INR leg is not?
options: Credit the exporter from the suspense account
Report it as In progress or Unknown until the INR leg confirms
questions.explanation: End-to-end completion requires all required leg confirmations. Until then the status stays In progress or Unknown and the item is investigated.
